issues.body: Section 6 P0 requires a T1-only crate and "the 35 migrated tests," while P2 later moves the IO/service tiers. The existing 35-test module includes tests for IdleTimeoutStream, MaxRequestsService, upgrade handling, acceptor/handshake behavior, and builder configuration, so those tests cannot compile in the T1-only crate. This also contradicts section 9's admission that the test split was not audited and makes the claimed disjoint phased plan invalid.
issues.fix_hint: Inventory the tests by tier and assign only policy/parser/limiter tests to P0; explicitly assign IO/service tests to P2 and builder/acceptor tests to P3. Replace the unsupported count with verified per-phase counts or omit counts, and make each phase's acceptance tests concrete.
issues.title: P0 cannot migrate all 35 tests into a T1-only crate

issues.body: Section 3.2 presents limiter.try_acquire() and limiter.try_acquire_ip() as the primary consumer API, then states that only PermittedStream::new is private and must be exposed. In the referenced implementation both ConnectionLimiter::try_acquire and ConnectionLimiter::try_acquire_ip are private (the latter has only a doc-hidden test shim). P1 therefore cannot use the shown seam across a crate boundary, and the design has not specified or reviewed the necessary public guard API.
issues.fix_hint: Correct the API delta and phase specs to include public, documented acquisition methods (and any guard construction/access needed for unknown peers), or design one public atomic admission method that returns the global and per-IP guards together. Include tests for fail-fast global admission, per-IP refusal, unknown-peer fail-open behavior, and release on guard drop.
issues.title: The hand-rolled accept-loop API needs more public surface than documented

verdict.summary: The design usefully corrects the issue premise, but its staged plan is not internally executable as written. P0 claims all 35 transport tests migrate with the T1-only crate even though many of those tests exercise T2-T4 types, and the proposed primary hand-loop API relies on limiter methods that are currently private despite the record claiming only one constructor needs exposure. These are load-bearing scope/API errors in the bead decomposition, not cosmetic wording.
